title: Telemetry compatibility matrix generator and runtime shim strategy
creator: Marco Li
description:
Problem: As the analytics schema and telemetry SDKs evolve, clients using different SDK/CLI/API versions send mixed payloads to our ingest pipelines. Current runtime feature gates require manual rules and ad-hoc transformations which lead to data loss, consumer breakages, and convoluted rollback paths.

Goal: Build a reproducible compatibility-matrix generator and a lightweight runtime shim (adapter) that can: (1) enumerate supported field-level compat between SDK/CLI/API versions and model them as an explicit matrix, (2) produce code and config artifacts used by ingest gateways to perform safe, minimal transformations, and (3) provide a canary-safe rollout and observability surface for regressions.

Scope: generator tool, ingest shim spec, tests for round-trip fidelity, CI gating, and a phased rollout plan for Console backend and public SDKs. Not in scope: full schema redesign or client SDK major-version bumps (those are separate initiatives).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix generator accepts a set of schema snapshots (JSON descriptors) and outputs a deterministic matrix CSV and JSON artifact describing per-field compatibility rules.
Runtime shim applies transformation rules with <0.5% additional p99 latency on our ingest path in a dedicated canary pool.
End-to-end tests validate that telemetry consumers (console analytics, billing pipelines) receive semantically equivalent records for supported transformations.
Rollout plan documented and tested via canary + gradual ramp with automatic rollback on quality/regression signals.
SDK/CLI release notes include adapter compatibility guarantees and a migration checklist for customers.
Automated CI check prevents merging schema changes that would cause unhandled-breaking transforms without an accompanying adapter rule.
Monitoring dashboards surface transform counts, dropped fields, and consumer error rates per version-pair.
Security review signoff for any transformation that involves redaction or PII handling.
design_notes:
We will represent schema snapshots as a normalized JSON descriptor (flattened field paths, types, optional/required, enum sets, deprecation markers). The generator computes a directed compatibility graph between two snapshots and emits per-field rules: passthrough, rename, type-coerce, enum-map, default-fill, drop. The ingest shim reads the JSON artifact and applies rules in request path prior to enrichment. To minimize latency, the shim will be implemented as a Rust library used by our ingest gateway service and exposed via an in-process transform hook. Rule evaluation is compiled to a compact decision table and cached per-schema-pair. For SDKs we provide a companion reporting hook to surface SDK version and declared capabilities in the event envelope.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Server-side transforms centralize control but increase operational coupling; 2) Client-side libraries reduce server work but require aggressive SDK adoption; 3) Full schema negotiation handshake (expensive) vs. artifact-driven transforms (faster rollout) — we choose artifact-driven with optional negotiation metadata for future compatibility.

Security: Any rule marked "redact" must be accompanied by a KMS-approved rationale and a short-lived retention exception. Redaction operations will be audited and logged separately.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Schema descriptor spec and canonicalizer + compatibility matrix generator PoC. Produce matrix artifacts for last 6 released telemetry schemas.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Rust ingest shim library prototype that reads matrix artifact, applies rules, and exposes a minimal API. Unit tests for all rule types and type coercions.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Integrate shim into ingest gateway in a canary region; add CI job to validate generator artifacts against consumer contracts.
Phase 4 (1 week): Observability and alerting: dashboards, transform telemetry, drop counts, consumer error spikes. Create runbook for rollback triggers.
Phase 5 (1 week): SDK/CLI companion telemetry hook and release notes + docs for partners. Finalize security review and compliance checklist.
Phase 6 (ongoing): Iterate on matrix heuristics and add auto-suggested enum mappings from historical payloads.
test_plan: Create synthetic corpus by replaying historical telemetry for N different SDK versions. For each schema-pair, run generator, apply shim, and assert consumer-level invariants: record completeness, no silent drops for required fields, and acceptable type coercion outcomes. Add property-based tests for enum mapping and round-trip idempotency. Establish performance benchmarks and assert <0.5% p99 overhead in canary. CI job will run a lightweight snapshot diff on schema changes and fail if incompatible-without-rule detected.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy generator and new artifacts to artifacts store. 2) Deploy shim to canary ingest pool limited to 1% traffic; monitor transform metrics for 48 hours. 3) Ramp to 10% then 50% with automated quality checks. 4) If regressions detected, automatic rollback to previous shim version and alert on-call. 5) Announce opt-in SDK flag that allows client-side pre-transform if users want to avoid server-side adaptations.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect enum mappings introduce semantic drift. Mitigation: require human review for all auto-suggested enum maps and flag high-volume changes for manual signoff.
Risk: Latency regression in ingest path. Mitigation: implement decision-table compilation and in-memory caching; run perf budgets in CI.
Risk: Operators misuse redact rules. Mitigation: gated RBAC and mandatory audit trail plus security review for redact rules.
Risk: Consumers downstream expect older fields; removal causes analytic gaps. Mitigation: provide virtual backfill tooling and mark transforms as reversible in artifacts where possible.
